Did you just visualize it or did you draw up prints? I've wanted to get into wood working.

I usually plan things out in Sketchup to get an idea of proportions and scale. I have plans for a lot more toys than I've built.

When building I use the plans as a guide, but some dimensions are a bit fluid. For example the width of the roller is determined by the overall width of the back axle, so I'll make the chassis and rear wheels first then maker the rest to fit.

I try to stick to a common scale so they make sense together. For these ones that is determined by a chassis made from 4x2 and wheels that are generally 3/4" thick.

These are beautiful. Almost anyone can follow directions and construct one of these. Where true craftsmanship and these pieces in particular stand out is on the finish work. Sanding and shaping is tedious.

It's also the difference in a clunky amateurish project and beautifly presented items like these.

They're not too hard to sand, I have a set of small sanding drums that go in my drill press. I usually use the largest one unless I need to get into a tight radius. The edges are knocked off with a chisel or spoke shave then sanded, I like the look that gives (for this series of toys), a bit whimsical. I finish pretty much all of my toys and other smallish wood projects using danish oil (I use Organoil Danish Oil, it has a nice citrus scent and brings out the grain in the wood really well. If your danish oil smells like solvents, find another one :-) ).

The tricky thing is the precision, it mostly comes with practice, but you need to be very precise with the placement and alignment of holes etc. A good drill press and vise help here.
